newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly steady, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly steady, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Wednesday in thin trade, with mild East Coast weather promising little change in utility demand though some felt prices had bottomed, industry sources said.
"There's no demand yet, but it's starting to feel like we're at or close to bottom," said one trader, noting recent firmer gas prices encouraged some switching to resid.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to $14.25-50 a barrel, with May one percent paper at $14.20-40 also losing some ground. Traders said June paper was quoted at $14.70-90, while July was pegged at $15.00-25.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was unchanged at $15.25, while high sulphurs in New York also showed little movement. Traders said NYH 2.2 percent was still talked in the low-$14 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices also were stable, with one percent still pegged on either side of $14.50 and three percent straddling $13.25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate gas prices edged up slightly to near the $2.40/mmBtu mark, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed by about five cents to $2.15/mmBtu, or $13.55 a barrel.
